title: Quedarse sin: perder algo de lo que se dependía

sections.content: Quedarse sin (to be left without, to run out of) describes suddenly lacking something previously relied on -- especially vivid for describing the abrupt loss of support, supplies, or resources. It's followed by a noun phrase. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Cuba se quedó sin esta ayuda prácticamente de un día para otro.
items.english: Cuba was left without this aid practically overnight.

items.spanish: Sin el petróleo barato soviético, la isla se quedó sin una fuente de energía fundamental para su economía.
items.english: Without cheap Soviet oil, the island was left without a fuel source fundamental to its economy.

items.spanish: Muchas fábricas se quedaron sin materias primas suficientes para continuar produciendo con normalidad.
items.english: Many factories were left without enough raw materials to keep producing normally.

items.spanish: El gobierno se quedó sin margen de maniobra para responder a esta crisis económica repentina.
items.english: The government was left without room to maneuver in responding to this sudden economic crisis.

sections.content: Quedarse sin emphasizes the sudden, often involuntary loss of something -- unlike carecer de, which simply states an ongoing lack without implying a specific moment when it began.
